scene.speaker: valentina
scene.bubble: The lake is like a mirror today! Let's take the little boat — and Erik, please don't bring inventions that sink.
scene.intro: The lake is like a mirror today. Let's take the little boat! says Valentina. Let's have the picnic on that rock! says Erik. They row to the middle of the water, with the forest behind them and the mountain over everything. A fish jumps twice, very close. Let's stay here for ever — but the sandwiches are already finished. What shall we do today? Choose a plan and say Let's!

activities.title: Grammar · Go for a swim!
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.

data.title: Let's go for a swim!
data.intro: You can go for a walk, a swim, a ride or a picnic. The action turns into a thing you go for — and the little a is never missing.
data.can: I can say go for a walk / a swim / a ride to talk about what we do outside.

examples.text: Yesterday we went for a drive in my brother's new car.
Let's go for a swim in the lake!
We went for a walk in the forest and saw a big rock.
Erik goes for a ride on his bike every Saturday.

rules: go / goes / went + for a + walk, swim, ride, drive, picnic.
Never "go for swim". The a always stays.
Go swimming is also correct — but then there is no for and no a.
